# ArrayColumnMissingField

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect array_column on a literal array of literal rows when at least one row has the requested literal field and at least one lacks it.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
array_column([["id"=>1],["name"=>"Ada"]],"id");
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Handle rows missing the selected field explicitly.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report array_column on a literal array of literal rows when at least one row has the requested literal field and at least one lacks it.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is disabled; enable only when the stated intent matches the application.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases or recursion cannot establish definite facts. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Do not report object rows, unknown keys, uniformly missing fields, or cases where field presence is unknown.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

## Fix

No automatic fix: whether to omit, reject, or substitute missing rows is an application decision.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ArrayColumnMissingField": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ArrayColumnMissingField
```
